title: Build a fixed-size ring buffer in Rust — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a ring buffer: turn 1 push/pop, turn 2 is_full/is_empty, turn 3 Iterator impl.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `push(&mut self, value: T) -> Result<(), T>` and `pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>` in `src/lib.rs`. push: if full return Err(value); else write to data[tail], advance tail with wrap-around (tail = (tail+1) % capacity), increment len. pop: if empty return None; else take data[head] (leave None), advance head with wrap-around, decrement len. Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `is_full(&self) -> bool` (len == capacity) and `is_empty(&self) -> bool` (len == 0). Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures — especially the wrap-around test.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All 5 tests must pass. The Iterator impl already delegates to pop(), so just make sure it compiles and runs.
success_criteria: is_full and is_empty reflect current len
Iterator collects all elements via pop
